description: Layout primitive for a grid of equal columns, such as a grid of cards. Columns are never narrower than 16rem and drop away as the grid narrows, so it needs no breakpoints; columns caps how many there are.

columns.description: The most columns to show. Without it, as many 16rem columns as fit.

gap.description: Spacing between rows and columns, from the intent spacing scale.

default.description: The grid items, one per cell.

handled: Purely presentational: adds no role, no landmark, and no tab stop. Items keep source order, so reading and tab order match the visual order.

required.when: the grid is a list of like items, such as project cards
required.requirement: Give it list semantics when the count matters to the reader: role="list" on aihio-grid and role="listitem" on each item.

counterExamples.reason: columns takes 2, 3, or 4. Six 16rem columns do not fit a typical content width, and the grid would drop them anyway.
A hand-rolled grid ignores the spacing scale and squeezes its columns on narrow screens. Use aihio-grid.

examples.title: Three columns of cards
examples.description: Columns drop away as the grid narrows, with no breakpoints.
